rationale.source: papermain.pdf ("Governed Compilation of AI Controls"), Section IX.C "Cases", Case C description
rationale.source_status: Manuscript prose is NOT scientific evidence (per this project's own evidentiary discipline); it is cited here only as the authorial statement of ORIGINAL SCOPE this reconciliation is checking the repository against -- the numeric claims within it are independently re-verified below, not taken on faith.
rationale.quote: Case C is released as a compiled package (16 risks, 13 authorized specifications, 16 compiled records—13 risk-derived and 3 compiler invariants—payload SHA-256 d7c79711...bf1dbd) passing the ten audit queries and twelve executable injections plus a clean control; it enters no determinism, cross-platform or Monte Carlo campaign, its gate-deficit figures are recomputed over the printed register rather than measured on the bundle, and no simulator or hardware execution is described or inferred.
rationale.summary: Case C (synthetic, standards-anchored supervised-autonomy surgical design case) is, by explicit original design, a compiled-and-audited artifact only. It was never intended to enter the determinism, cross-platform/CI, or Monte Carlo campaigns that Case A, Case B v1.1, and Case D CCS0/CCS1/CCS2 do. Its gate-deficit figures are a register-level recomputation over the printed risk register, not a measurement taken on the compiled bundle. Adding Case C to the v1.2 determinism/CI/Monte Carlo protocol would extend the original scope, not close a gap in it -- so gap-audit item 9 is classified NOT_REQUIRED rather than forced.
